info.title: Smart Grid Asset Management API

get.description: One page of every stored asset, ordered by asset id unless `sort` says otherwise, optionally filtered by text (case-insensitive substring of the id or name), asset type and operational status. `total` counts all matches across pages.

parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Only assets in this operational status (see GET /api/lookups)
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Column to order by; ties and the default are by asset id. Assets with no parent sort last.
parameters.name: sort

400.description: Unknown type, status or sort, or bad dir/limit/offset

get.description: Every asset that has no parent (substations), each with `child_count` and `subtree_count` so a tree can render expanders without further requests.

Case-insensitive substring match on asset id or name, optionally restricted to one asset type. Exact id matches come first, then id prefixes. `%` and `_` in `q` are matched literally. Results are capped at `limit`; `truncated` says whether more matched.

parameters.description: Text to look for in the asset id or name
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: Only assets of this type (see GET /api/lookups)
parameters.name: type

400.description: Missing q, unknown type, or bad limit

get.description: The total number of stored assets and how many there are of each asset type and each operational status. Types and statuses with no assets are omitted.
get.summary: Count assets by type and status

get.description: Every stored attribute of the asset.

delete.description: Removes an asset that has no children. An asset that still has children is refused with 409 and must have them deleted first. See docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md.

403.description: No API key is configured on the server, so the API is disabled

409.description: The asset has children, or another writer collided with the delete

get.description: The path from the top of the hierarchy down to the asset, in that order; the asset itself is the last element. Use it to expand a tree to a search hit.

The asset's immediate children grouped by asset type (each with `child_count` and `subtree_count`), plus `descendant_counts`: how many descendants of each type sit anywhere beneath the asset. An asset with no children returns empty lists.

One page of import activity, newest first: file name, client IP, row counts and whether data was committed. Imports only — deletions are not listed. Fetch `GET /api/imports/{importId}` for a run's rejected rows.

post.description:
Uploads a CSV of grid assets, validates every row again, and stores the rows that pass in one transaction. Rejected rows, and any row beneath a rejected parent, are skipped and reported; rows whose `asset_id` already exists are rejected, never updated. `committed` is true when at least one row was stored.

To let a user review the outcome first, call `POST /api/imports/preview` and send its `fingerprint` here as `expected_fingerprint`: if the file or the stored data changed since, nothing is written and the response is **412**. Without `expected_fingerprint` the rows that pass are stored directly.

**Columns are matched by header name**, in any order (case, spaces, `-` and `_` are ignored: `Asset ID` = `asset_id`). Required: `asset_id`, `asset_type`, `asset_name`, `operational_status`. Optional (may be absent from the file or blank): `parent_asset_id`, `voltage_kv`, `rating_kva`, `manufacturer`, `model`, `serial_number`, `commissioned_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `D/M/YYYY` or `D/M/YY`, day first). Unknown columns are ignored and listed in `ignored_columns`. Allowed asset types, statuses and parent/child pairings are read from the database — see `GET /api/lookups`.

A file that is readable but has bad rows returns **200** with `rejections[]`; `csv_row` is the row's line in the uploaded file (header = line 1). A file that cannot be processed at all (not CSV, empty, required column missing) returns a 4xx `ErrorResponse` instead.
post.summary: Import assets from a CSV file

parameters.description: CSV file with a header row
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: Fingerprint from POST /api/imports/preview for this file
parameters.name: expected_fingerprint

400.description: No file supplied, or the file is empty / has no data rows

409.description: Another writer changed the stored data during the commit; nothing was stored, retry

412.description: expected_fingerprint no longer matches; nothing was stored, preview again

413.description: File larger than the configured upload limit

415.description: File does not have a .csv extension

422.description: Malformed CSV (see `line`), or the header lacks a required column

post.description:
Validates the file exactly as `POST /api/imports` would and reports how many rows can be imported and which are rejected and why, **without storing anything** (no assets, no import record). Show this to the user, then confirm by sending the same file to `POST /api/imports` with `expected_fingerprint` set to the `fingerprint` returned here.

Column rules, date formats (`YYYY-MM-DD`, `D/M/YYYY`, `D/M/YY`, day first) and structural errors are the same as for the import.
post.summary: Check a CSV file without importing it

parameters.description: CSV file with a header row
parameters.name: file

400.description: No file supplied, or the file is empty / has no data rows

413.description: File larger than the configured upload limit

415.description: File does not have a .csv extension

422.description: Malformed CSV (see `line`), or the header lacks a required column

get.description: A CSV with every importable column in its header and a few fictional example rows (a small valid hierarchy) showing how parents, dates and statuses are written. Delete the example rows before importing your own data.
Re-fetches the result of an earlier import, including every rejected row. `ignored_columns` is only reported on the upload response and is empty here.

The asset types, operational statuses and parent/child type pairings that imports are validated against, read from the database (refreshed on startup and on every import). Use it to build filters and dropdowns instead of hardcoding values.
Returns service liveness and DB connectivity status.

total.description: Total is the number of assets matching the filters, across all pages.

child_count.description: ChildCount is the number of immediate children (0 = leaf).

rating_kva.description:
RatingKVA and CommissionedDate let a list of nodes (the children of an
asset) be sorted without a request per row. CommissionedDate is YYYY-MM-DD.

subtree_count.description:
SubtreeCount is the number of assets in this asset's subtree,
including the asset itself (a leaf has 1).

count.description: Count is the number of immediate children of this type.

subtree_count.description:
SubtreeCount is the combined subtree size of those children
(each child counted with its own descendants).

error.description:
Error is a human-readable, user-safe message. For 5xx it is generic —
internals are only ever written to the server log.

line.description: Line is the 1-indexed source line of a structurally malformed CSV, when known.

trace_id.description:
TraceID matches the X-Trace-Id response header and the server log lines
for this request; quote it when reporting a 5xx.

fingerprint.description:
Fingerprint is a SHA-256 hex digest of the file's cells and of the
validation outcome.

ignored_columns.description: IgnoredColumns lists header columns the importer does not recognise.

IgnoredColumns lists header columns the importer does not recognise;
they are skipped (not an error) and not stored.

root_types.description: RootTypes are asset types with no parent rule: they must have no parent.

csv_row.description:
CSVRow is the row's original 1-indexed line in the uploaded file
(the header is line 1), not its position after any reordering.

reason.description: Reason holds every problem found on the row, joined with "; ".

truncated.description: Truncated is true when more assets matched than limit allowed.

type.description: Type echoes the applied asset_type filter ("" = none).

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key (see API_KEY in .env). Required by every /api endpoint (sent as the x-api-key header). Only /healthz and these docs are open. This is a shared key, not user authentication (see ARCHITECTURE.md).
ApiKeyAuth.name: x-api-key
